nodes.text: Mind the furrows. What brings you out to the dirt?

choices.text: You weren't always town farmers, were you?

nodes.text: Crofted out east once, past the hedges — good soil, bad neighbors. Bandit autumn came through and burnt the barn with the season in it. We watched from the treeline. Tamsin's cousins still work the *Fernway* verges — crofter stock doesn't quit, it just picks better walls. Ours are Amberford's now, and I sleep like a plough in winter.

Wheat for Garton, carrots for Merra, cotton if Tamsin wins — and she will, she's already talked to the soil behind my back. Everything this town eats starts in one of three places, and I'm standing on the biggest. No grander work anywhere, whatever the mountain thinks.
Walk soft on the seed rows. Everything else forgives boots.
